links.note: Answered 'average income or per capita income', which is 23761's description (total income divided by population). 23760 is the prior claim that income is WHY countries are compared at all; this stem asks for the measure itself.
Sri Lanka outperforming India on human development is an HDI-ranking fact, 23763.
Arithmetic on average income - four families, a per capita income of 5,000, three incomes given. That is 23761's formula being applied.
The World Bank's criterion and its limitations - per capita income thresholds from the World Development Report, and averages hiding disparities. Both halves are 23761's description.
UNDP's criterion against the World Bank's: HDI combining health, education and income versus per capita income alone. 23763.
Why averages are used and what they hide - 23761, which carries both the definition and the caveat that averages conceal disparities.

Kerala ranking higher on human development than Punjab despite lower per capita income is explained by its health and education indicators, which is 23762 (measuring development where income cannot). 23763 is the index that aggregates them, tested by qid:87360 and qid:87357.

Present energy sources and what they will be in fifty years; the answer's point is that the conventional sources will not last. 23766, resources running out. 23767 is the sustainability principle drawn from it.
Why sustainability matters for development - balancing use against conservation for the future. 23767's description.
'Enough for all needs, not for one person's greed' answered through reckless exploitation leading to exhaustion of resources - 23766.

Examples of environmental degradation observed around one (deforestation, falling groundwater, soil erosion, pollution, the ozone hole). Degradation is the threat to development continuing across generations, 23767; 23766 is specifically about stocks running out.
The table is the HDI components set for India and its neighbours - per capita income, life expectancy, literacy, gross enrolment and HDI rank - so 23763, the index that combines them.

Undernourishment despite enough food in the country; the answer turns on the Public Distribution System, i.e. whether public facilities are provided and function. 23765. 23762 would fit a question about the nutrition statistic as an indicator, but the explanation asked for is the provisioning failure.
'Average income is the same as per capita income' is 23761's definition; the three wrong options misstate it as total income, as employed people's income, or as including property.
A developed country identified as one among the highest on the Human Development Index, against the distractors that rely on wealth alone. 23763.
Protection from infectious disease and a pollution-free atmosphere as the things money cannot buy is 23764's description almost verbatim; a luxury home and paid-for education are what it can.
Solar as the promising source BECAUSE it is not exhaustible - the reasoning is exhaustibility, which is 23766. 23767 covers the intergenerational principle rather than which stocks run out.

Rising vehicle exhaust as the cause that enhances environmental degradation, against tree planting, effluent control and a plastics ban. Environmental degradation belongs with 23767, as does qid:87366.
Which component matters most for comparing countries - income, against population and resources. That is 23760, income as the criterion of comparison; 23761 is the per-capita form and its limits.

Features of a developing country (agriculture-dominated, mass poverty, mass illiteracy) against high technological development. The developed/developing division in this chapter comes from the World Bank's per-capita-income classification, which 23761 holds; no concept in this frame lists developing-country characteristics directly.

Asks the most important attribute for comparing countries' development - 23760, income. DEFECT: the key is 'None of these', but the chapter says income is one of the most important attributes for comparison, so option C (average income) is correct. The duplicate qid:105732 keys per capita income, contradicting this row.
